newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool sees 20 mln T crop.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool sees 20 mln T crop.

text.p: The seven major grains and oilseeds grown in Saskatchewan should yield 20 million tonnes in 1997/98 (Aug/July), Saskatchewan Wheat Pool's chief executive Don Loewen told Reuters.
Saskatchewan Agriculture on July 29 forecast wheat, oats, barley, rye, flax and canola output in 1997/98 (Aug/July) to yield 22.34 million tonnes.
The 10.5 percent decline in crop production prospects was due to drought conditions throughout the province's grainbelt, Loewen said in an interview.

"We have an average crop at best. Some crops are very good and some are very bad because we got so little rain in July," he said. "There's great crops in the heavier soil zones that hold more water but the lighter land couldn't handle all that heat."
The 1987 to 1996 average crop output for Saskatchewan is 21.45 million tonnes, Saskatchewan Agriculture figures show.
